name: Cryogenic impact milling of a crystalline drug under liquid nitrogen for 2.5 h at 9 impacts per second to produce the amorphous form
plain_name: Grind a medicine into powder while liquid nitrogen keeps it brittle
description: Crystalline bosentan is milled in a stainless-steel grinding vessel immersed in liquid nitrogen in a Retsch CryoMill at an impact frequency of 9 cycles per second for a total of 2.5 h, converting it to the amorphous state without the thermal degradation that ambient milling or melt-quenching would cause. The amorphous product is then compared with the melt-quenched glass.
keywords: Grind a medicine into powder while liquid nitrogen keeps it brittle

sources.citation: A. Minecka, K. Chmiel, K. Jurkiewicz, et al., Studies on the Vitrified and Cryomilled Bosentan, Molecular Pharmaceutics 19(1):80-90 (2022)
RETSCH GmbH CryoMill equipment data sheet, reproduced on AZoM (equipment ID 9856)

reported_equipment: CryoMill ~100-240 V-50/60 Hz, Retsch GmbH, Germany

requirements.rationale: The grinding jar is held at liquid-nitrogen temperature (-196 C = 77150 mK) throughout, which is what embrittles the drug and stops it recrystallising or degrading during milling.
The procedure consumes liquid nitrogen: the milling vessel is physically immersed in it, so a purely mechanical or electrically cooled machine cannot reproduce the process.
The machine has to be a cryogenic impact mill: the amorphisation comes from mechanical impact delivered while the sample is at cryogenic temperature.
Milling was carried out at 9 impacts per second (9 Hz), which must lie inside the mill's selectable frequency range.
Full amorphisation needed 2.5 h (9000 s) of milling, so the machine's programmable grinding time (with intermediate cooling cycles) must reach that total.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
